title: KC DE Research Method
bodyHtml:
What is differential expression analysis?

Differential Expression (DE) analysis identifies genes whose expression differs among tissues or phenotypes. By identifying putative expression biomarkers, DE analyses can inform hypothesis generation and further exploration of Common Fund or user-generated data.

Input data

Differential Expression currently includes human bulk RNA sequencing data from the following Common Fund programs:

GTEx

  • 980 adult donors
  • 54 tissues
  • Phenotypes include common metabolic diseases, age-related phenotypes, and more

 Kids First

  • 1443 pediatric and adult donors
  • 2 tissues
  • Phenotypes include congenital heart defects, Down syndrome, and pediatric cancers

Analysis methods

We performed differential expression analyses to identify genes associated with available trait and disease phenotypes. For the GTEx consortium, we extracted gene counts in 54 tissues from version 8 of GTEx data processing as well as phenotypes for each donor. For KidsFirst, we extracted gene counts for peripheral blood and bone marrow from data processing with Kallisto as well as phenotypes for each donor. We excluded genes with low median expression and high variability in expression across donors. For each tissue, then we performed differential gene expression analyses of each phenotype using the Wald test in DESeq2. Phenotypes are annotated using the Mondo Disease Ontology and the Human Phenotype Ontology. The tests included where available, sample covariates age, BMI, and biological sex as well as technical covariates ischemia time, fixation method, and isolation method. The resulting p-values were corrected for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method. The results were filtered to remove immunoglobulin genes, which have high genetic diversity and expression variability which may lead to spurious associations, and genes not tested for association. Finally, genes were considered significant at FDR<0.10.

Representation of results on the KC portal

Differential expression results are represented in volcano plots of the log2-transformed fold change of the mean expression of the gene (x-axis) relative to the negative log10-transformed adjusted p-value (y-axis). Higher fold change values indicate greater differential expression of the gene; negative or positive values indicate downregulation or upregulation of the gene, respectively. Adjusted p-values indicate statistical significance, with lower values indicating more significant differential expression.

Log2-transformed fold change values >0.5 or <-0.5 are considered significant; negative log10-transformed adjusted p-values >1.3 are statistically significant.

What's next?

We'll be adding additional datasets for enhanced differential expression analyses, and users will soon be able to bring their own results for custom analysis. Stay tuned!
